newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific Railroad CEO resigns.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific Railroad CEO resigns.

text.p: Union Pacific Corp. said Wednesday Ronald Burns has resigned as chief executive officer and president of Union Pacific Railroad Co.
Union Pacific spokesman Gary Schuster declined to comment on the company's statement, which noted Burns, 44, joined the Omaha, Neb.-based railroad in August of 1995 from Enron Corp.
The company named Jerry Davis, 58, president of Southern Pacific Rail Lines, as president and chief operating officer of the railroad.
Dick Davidson, president and chief operating officer of Union Pacific Corp. and chairman of the railroad, was named chief executive.
Davidson is scheduled to become chairman and chief executive of Union Pacific Corp. on Jan. 1, succeeding Drew Lewis, the company said.
Davis served as executive vice president of operations at Union Pacific Railroad when it merged with the Missouri Pacific in 1983.
"We are very fortunate to have someone with Jerry's working knowledge of the Union Pacific and Southern Pacific rail systems to step in as we merge the two lines," Lewis said.

Davis left Union Pacific in 1989 to become president of CSX Corp.'s CSX Rail Transport. In 1995, Davis joined Southern Pacific as its president and chief executive, where he remained until the Union Pacific/Southern Pacific merger was completed on Sept. 11.
